title: Practice 1: To whom: giving, telling, showing

blocks.text: Exercises: sentences from Tatoeba (tatoeba.org, CC BY 2.0 FR) and from the library's public-domain books.

exercises.q: Брат сказал ___ (брат): то мое, а это мое же!
exercises.why: After the verb давать-дать the object given is in the accusative case; the person to whom the object is given is in the dative case: *Он даст словарь сыну.* After посылать-послать the object sent is in the accusative case; the person to whom the object is sent is in the dative case: *Я пошлю книгу брату.* After говорить-сказать the person to whom something is said is in the dative case: *Я скажу ему, что вы уже здесь.* — From the Wikibooks Russian textbook (CC BY-SA 4.0). From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 28, 39.  ·  «The dative case is used mostly to denote the person to whom something is given, sent, told, shown, etc.» — DLI, Lesson 28.
exercises.context: After the verb давать-дать the object given is in the accusative case; the person to whom the object is given is in the dative case: *Он даст словарь сыну.* After посылать-послать the object sent is in the accusative case;…

From the DLI Grammar Reference Book. Lessons 28, 39.  ·  «The dative case is used mostly to denote the person to whom something is given, sent, told, shown, etc.» — DLI, Lesson 28.
